spain-1996.title: Barcelona, 1996: first win in red, in the rain
spain-1996.summary: In torrential rain at the Circuit de Catalunya, Michael Schumacher scored his first victory for Ferrari. He recovered from a poor start, led from lap 12 and won by 45.3 seconds from Jean Alesi.

captions.text: A clutch problem at the start drops Schumacher from third on the grid to sixth. Villeneuve leads.
Schumacher passes Alesi for second, braking late and diving inside the Benetton.
Schumacher takes the lead from Villeneuve and at times pulls away by four seconds a lap.
captions.note: Wikipedia gives lap 13 for this pass; Autosport and Jolpica lap positions give lap 12.

captions.text: First pit stop. Schumacher rejoins still in the lead.
Second and final stop. The Ferrari keeps the lead comfortably.
Chequered flag: Schumacher wins by 45.3 seconds from Alesi, with Villeneuve third. His first Ferrari victory.

japan-2000.title: Suzuka, 2000: the drought ends
japan-2000.summary: Michael Schumacher beat Mika Häkkinen by 1.8 seconds, taking the lead at his final pit stop. The win made him 2000 world champion, Ferrari's first drivers' champion since Jody Scheckter in 1979.
japan-2000.conditions: Dry and overcast, with light rain in the second half

captions.text: Häkkinen out-drags pole-sitter Schumacher into the first corner and leads by eight-tenths after one lap.
Häkkinen makes his first pit stop; Schumacher leads for one lap.
Schumacher pits a lap later and rejoins behind Häkkinen after a slightly longer stop.
Light rain makes the track slippery, though not enough for wet tyres. Schumacher closes in.
Häkkinen makes his second stop. Schumacher, now leading, stays out on a light fuel load.
Schumacher's final stop: he rejoins 4.1 seconds ahead of Häkkinen and keeps the lead.
Schumacher wins by 1.8 seconds and is world champion: Ferrari's first drivers' title since 1979.

france-2004.title: Magny-Cours, 2004: four stops to victory
france-2004.summary: Unable to pass pole-sitter Fernando Alonso on track, Ferrari switched Michael Schumacher to a four-stop strategy and he won by 8.3 seconds. Rubens Barrichello took third on the final lap.

captions.text: Alonso keeps the lead from pole; Schumacher follows in second.
Schumacher is first to pit, at the end of lap 11. Alonso stays out until lap 14.
A short-fuelled second stop commits Schumacher to four stops. He starts setting a series of fastest laps.
captions.note: Wikipedia gives lap 28; the formula1.com pit stop summary and article give lap 29.

captions.text: Alonso makes his second stop and loses the lead to Schumacher.
Third stop for Schumacher. Alonso leads until his final stop on lap 46.
captions.note: Wikipedia gives lap 45 for Alonso's last stop; formula1.com gives lap 46.

captions.text: Fourth stop. Schumacher rejoins still ahead of Alonso.
captions.note: Wikipedia gives lap 57; the formula1.com pit stop summary gives lap 58.

captions.text: Schumacher wins by 8.3 seconds. Barrichello passes Trulli on the final lap for third.

brazil-2007.title: Interlagos, 2007: champion by one point
brazil-2007.summary: Kimi Räikkönen arrived third in the standings, seven points behind Lewis Hamilton, and won the race ahead of teammate Felipe Massa. Hamilton finished seventh, and Räikkönen took the title by a single point.

captions.text: Massa leads from pole. Räikkönen passes Hamilton for second; Hamilton runs wide and drops to eighth.
Hamilton's McLaren slips into neutral and slows; he falls to 18th.
captions.note: Autosport's lap-by-lap puts this at lap 7; Jolpica lap times and positions show the slow lap and the drop to 18th on lap 8.

captions.text: Massa makes his first stop and Räikkönen leads. The Finn pits a lap later.
Massa makes his second stop. Räikkönen, running light, takes the lead with a run of fast laps.
Räikkönen's final stop. He rejoins in the lead, about two seconds ahead of Massa.
Räikkönen wins by 1.5 seconds and is world champion by one point from Hamilton and Alonso.

italy-2019.title: Monza, 2019: red at home again
italy-2019.summary: Charles Leclerc converted pole into victory, holding off Lewis Hamilton and then Valtteri Bottas. It was Ferrari's first Italian Grand Prix win since 2010.

captions.text: Leclerc converts pole into the lead; Hamilton and Bottas follow.
Vettel, running fourth, spins alone at Ascari and drops to the back. He later receives a stop-go penalty.
Leclerc pits for hard tyres, a lap after Hamilton, and rejoins just ahead of the Mercedes.
Leclerc forces Hamilton onto the run-off at the second chicane and is shown the black-and-white flag.
captions.note: formula1.com says 'two laps later' after Leclerc emerged on lap 21, which gives lap 23; no source states the lap number directly.

captions.text: Bottas's lap 27 stop hands the lead back to Leclerc.
Hamilton locks up at Turn 1 and Bottas takes second to chase Leclerc on fresher tyres.
Leclerc wins by 0.835 seconds from Bottas: Ferrari's first win at Monza since 2010.

barcelona-2026.title: Barcelona, 2026: Hamilton's first win in red
barcelona-2026.summary: Lewis Hamilton won on a three-stop strategy, using a Virtual Safety Car to make his final stop and keep the lead. It was his first Grand Prix win for Ferrari, 19.6 seconds ahead of George Russell.

captions.text: Pole-sitter Russell holds the lead into Turn 1. Hamilton, second on the grid on soft tyres, stays second.
Hamilton is first of the front-runners to pit, switching from soft to hard tyres.
captions.note: formula1.com's report and Wikipedia place the first stops 'at the Lap 12 mark' or 'around lap 12'; the official pit stop summary gives lap 11.

captions.text: A second stop, for medium tyres, commits Hamilton to three stops and undercuts the Mercedes.
captions.note: Wikipedia gives lap 28; the formula1.com pit stop summary gives lap 27.

captions.text: Russell and Antonelli make their second stops, leaving Hamilton in the lead.
Alonso stops on track. Under the Virtual Safety Car, Hamilton makes his third stop and keeps the lead.
captions.note: Ferrari's report puts the Virtual Safety Car on lap 40; Wikipedia and the pit stop summary give lap 41 for Hamilton's stop.

captions.text: Antonelli passes Russell for second but damages his car and retires. Leclerc also retires, bringing a second Virtual Safety Car.
Hamilton wins by 19.6 seconds, his first Ferrari victory. Russell and Norris complete the first all-British podium since 1968.
